_note: Protocol fixed before any robustness computation. Scenario hypothesis, not a probability distribution, a damage estimate or a confidence interval. lambda = 1, so the cost is C(w) = sum_i w_i e_i over 18 components: e_i counts attacks of class c classified as Normal (weight cost_fn of c) and Normal traffic classified as class c (weight cost_fp of c), for the 9 attack classes. Attack-to-attack confusions stay counted and unweighted. Each weight moves independently in [(1 - delta) w0_i, (1 + delta) w0_i]; independent moves can change the order of the costs between classes, and that limit is declared, not removed.
components: fn:<class> = cost_fn, fp:<class> = cost_fp, for every class except Normal, in label order

pairwise.worst_case: max_w w.(e_m - e_k) = w0.(e_m - e_k) + delta * sum_i w0_i |e_mi - e_ki|
pairwise.radius: -(w0.d) / sum_i w0_i |d_i| when w0.d <= 0 and the denominator is positive; m is not costlier than k for every delta <= radius and strictly better for every delta < radius; denominator zero means equal cost for every w; w0.d > 0 means no radius
pairwise.extreme_vector: w_i = w0_i (1 + delta * sign(d_i)), d_i = 0 left at w0_i

selection.rule: argmin over the pool of the maximum regret R_m(delta) = max(0, max_k [w0.(e_m - e_k) + delta * sum_i w0_i |e_mi - e_ki|]), computed exactly in rational arithmetic on delta_range
tie_break: lowest nominal validation cost at lambda = 1
fixed order lgbm, xgb, rf, logreg
compared_with: nominal choice: argmin of the validation cost at lambda = 1, same tie-break
macro-F1 choice: argmax of macro_f1_validation, ties in the fixed order

test: already examined in the baseline: computed after the selection, descriptive and retrospective only; it never enters the selection, the hypotheses or the tie-break
